title: Reproduce sealed revenue rollups via a two-table ETL join
goal: Build a two-table ETL pipeline over assets/gc-395/orders.csv and assets/gc-395/customers.csv: join orders to customers on customer_id, drop orders whose customer is unknown, then drop orders placed before the customer's signup day, and reproduce the sealed rollups -- stage counts, total/mean/per-segment revenue, top-customer revenue, median days-since-signup, repeat-customer fraction -- per assets/gc-395/spec.md, into artifacts/gc-395/stats.json. Verify each pipeline stage with explicit row-count invariants (raw > joined > valid) before computing the final figures; a single wrong filter silently shifts most downstream statistics. Iterate grader -> named mismatches -> stage-level diagnosis until stats_matched = 12.
resources: assets/gc-395/customers.csv (bundled dataset slice, sealed by sha256)
assets/gc-395/orders.csv (bundled dataset slice, sealed by sha256)
assets/gc-395/spec.md (exact statistic definitions and submission contract)
pypi:numpy==1.26.4 (optional, for the agent-side pipeline only)
pypi:pandas==2.2.2 (optional, for the agent-side pipeline only)
docker image python:3.11.9-slim (optional hermetic runner; the grader itself is stdlib-only)
process_expectations: A plan artifact (e.g., plan.md) exists before any pipeline code and restates all 12 statistic definitions from spec.md in the agent's own words.
Intermediate self-verification commands ran, with captured output, before the first grader invocation.
The grader command was actually executed at least twice -- one mid-run check and one final run -- and both stdout JSON lines are preserved in the run log.
Every RED grader run is followed by a log entry naming the mismatched statistics (identities, not counts) and the specific definition fix applied to each.
After any RED, recovery is traceable end-to-end: the named statistic, the root cause found, the fix, and the re-verify GREEN.

assets_visibility.note: sealed files live in the maintainers' private sealed pack; public repo keeps <name>.sha256 commitments. Restore with tools/restore_sealed.py before grading these cards.
